To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a vocabulary size of 100k words is sufficient to achieve good performance, (ii) randomized trees outperform other quantization methods, (iii) a spatial verification stage can be used to improve search quality, (iv) the spatial verification stage has diminishing returns as vocabulary size increases and (v) the quantization and spatial verification stages are complementary

(1) randomized trees are an effective and fast method for quantization, (2) the spatial verification stage is a useful and fast way to re-rank query results and (3) the combination of randomized trees and the spatial verification stage results in a system that is fast and scalable, and outperforms the state-of-the-art in large-scale object retrieval

(1) we show the importance of quantization in large-scale object retrieval; (2) we show the benefits of a spatial verification stage in large-scale object recognition; (3) we show the scalability of our system to large-scale object recognition.
